::: {.lead}
Today you improve a short talk in PowerPoint, like in a lab. Each
experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in PowerPoint on the lab computer.
**Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its
QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result
in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a computer with PowerPoint (the desktop app, or PowerPoint
  on the web at `office.com`) and the start file.
- **No lab computer today?** Your teacher does Part A on the screen, on the
  simulators of the interactive lesson. Do Part B on your phone.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · Slides, layouts and a theme

**The idea:** a presentation is a set of **slides**. A **layout** sets the
places on a slide (**placeholders**) for the title, the text and the
pictures: Title Slide, Title and Content, Two Content. A **theme** (Design
tab) gives the whole talk one look: colours, fonts and background; a
**variant** changes only its colours. Keep a strong contrast: dark text on
a light background, or light on dark. **F5** starts the slide show.

**Aim:** choose a layout, give the talk one look, and start the show.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Open `talk-start.pptx` (click **Enable Editing** if you see it). Click
   slide 1 and open **Home › Layout**: its layout is marked. Then click
   slide 3 and choose **Home › New Slide › Two Content**. Type the title
   *Before and after*.

   {{< record "Slide 1 has the layout … ; the new slide has … placeholders" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Slide 1 has the layout **Title Slide**: a big title and a subtitle. The
   new slide has **3 placeholders**: the title and two content boxes side
   by side. You click in a placeholder and type.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="3" unit="placeholders" hint="Count the title and the boxes side by side."}
   How many placeholders does the new **Two Content** slide have?

   Why: The title and two content boxes side by side.
   :::

2. On the **Design** tab, click a theme that you like, then two **Variants**,
   one after the other. Press **F5**, click through the talk, and press
   **Esc**.

   {{< record "The theme changed … slides ; a variant changes …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **All four slides** change their colours, fonts and background at once:
   a theme gives the whole talk one look. A **variant** changes only the
   colours. F5 starts the show from slide 1; Esc stops it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You click a theme. Which slides change?

   - [x] all the slides of the talk

     Why: A theme gives the whole talk one look.

   - [ ] only the slide that you clicked

     Why: A theme is for the whole presentation.

   - [ ] only the title slide

     Why: Every slide gets the new colours and fonts.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/slide-builder.html" poster="sims/slide-builder.png" title="Slide Builder: one good slide" >}}

3. In **Slide Builder**, do the five tasks: the layout Title and Content, a
   short title, 3 to 5 short points, a theme, and the picture with its alt
   text. Which layout do you choose?

   {{< record "The layout … ; my title …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Title and Content**: a title and one box for the points. A good title
   has 8 words or fewer, for example "New shop hours".
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Easy or hard to read from two metres? Sort the slides.

   Easy to read: a strong contrast
   :   dark text on a light background

       Why: A strong contrast: every word is clear.

   :   light text on a dark background

       Why: Also a strong contrast.

   Hard to read: a weak contrast
   :   light grey text on a white background

       Why: The text almost disappears.

   :   dark blue text on a black background

       Why: Two dark colours: a weak contrast.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Few words and notes

**The idea:** the audience listens to you; the slide only helps. Keep **3 to
5 points**, each with about **8 words or fewer**. Put the details that you
will say in the **speaker notes** (View › Notes): in the slide show, only
you see them (Presenter View).

**Aim:** keep few words on the slide, and put the rest in the notes.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Click slide 2, *Small changes at home*. Count its points. Then select
   its text (**Ctrl + A**, **Ctrl + C**), open **View › Notes**, and paste
   the text into the notes pane under the slide.

   {{< record "Points: … ; the text is now also in …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **6 points**, the longest with **18 words**: too much text for the back
   of the room. The long text is now also in the **notes pane**, where it
   keeps the details that you will say.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="6" unit="points" hint="Count the lines that start with a bullet."}
   How many points has slide 2 of `talk-start.pptx`?

   Why: 6 points, the longest with 18 words: too much text for one slide.
   :::

2. Now make the slide short: keep **3 to 5 points**, each with **8 words or
   fewer**.

   {{< record "My shortest point" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good result, for example: "Close the tap while you brush", "Fix a
   dripping tap", "Take a short shower", "Use a bucket for the car". The
   details stay in the notes.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   A good point for the slide, or too long? Sort them.

   Good: 8 words or fewer
   :   Close the tap while you brush

       Why: Six short words: easy to read.

   :   Fix a dripping tap

       Why: Four words: clear and short.

   Too long: keep it in the notes
   :   When you brush your teeth, please remember to close the tap so the water does not run

       Why: Seventeen words: say it, and keep it in the notes.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/slide-doctor.html" poster="sims/slide-doctor.png" title="Slide Doctor: fix the slide" kind="game" >}}

3. Play **Slide Doctor**: each slide of the Sunrise team has one problem;
   choose the best fix. What is the fix for a slide with a long paragraph?

   {{< record "The fix for a long paragraph: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Short points on the slide, the details in the notes**: the audience
   reads a few words and listens to you.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A slide has a paragraph of 60 words. What is the best fix?

   - [x] Keep 3 to 5 short points, and move the details to the notes.

     Why: Few words on the slide; you say the rest.

   - [ ] Make the font smaller, so that everything fits.

     Why: A small font is hard to read from the back of the room.

   - [ ] Read the paragraph aloud from the slide.

     Why: The audience reads faster than you speak and stops listening.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A transition and an animation

**The idea:** a **transition** is the move from one slide to the next
(Transitions tab); use one quiet transition, the same on every slide. An
**animation** moves one thing on a slide (Animations tab): **Appear** with
**By Paragraph** shows the points one by one, on each click. Few, quiet
effects keep the eyes on your message.

**Aim:** add one quiet transition to every slide, and show points one by
one.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. On the **Transitions** tab, choose **Fade**, set the **Duration** to
   **00.70**, and click **Apply To All**. Look at the thumbnails.

   {{< record "Next to every thumbnail: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A **small star** appears next to every thumbnail: each slide now has a
   transition. Apply To All gave every slide the same quiet Fade.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   After **Apply To All**, what appears next to every thumbnail?

   - [x] a small star

     Why: The star shows that the slide has a transition.

   - [ ] a number

     Why: Numbers mark animations on a slide, not transitions.

   - [ ] nothing

     Why: PowerPoint marks each slide that has a transition.
   :::

2. Click slide 3, *What we do at the office*. Click in its three points and
   choose **Animations › Appear**, then **Effect Options › By Paragraph**.
   Press **F5**, click until the end of slide 3, and press **Esc**.

   {{< record "Numbers next to the points … ; on each click …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **1, 2 and 3**, one next to each point: the order of the clicks. In the
   show, the slide fades in with its title, then **one point comes on each
   click**.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   In the slide show, put what comes on slide 3 in order.

   1. The slide fades in, with its title.
   2. Click: the first point appears.
   3. Click: the second point appears.
   4. Click: the third point appears.

   Why: The transition brings the slide; By Paragraph brings one point on each click.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/transition-lab.html" poster="sims/transition-lab.png" title="Transition Lab: transitions and animations" >}}

3. In **Transition Lab**, try the transitions Appear, Fade and Spin, then an
   animation By Paragraph. Which transition is too much for a talk?

   {{< record "Too much: … ; why …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Spin**: a big, loud effect takes the eyes from your message. A quiet
   Fade, the same on every slide, is enough.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which transitions fit a talk best?

   - [x] one quiet transition, the same on every slide

     Why: The audience watches your message, not the effects.

   - [ ] a different loud effect on every slide

     Why: Many effects take the eyes from your message.

   - [ ] Spin on every slide

     Why: Spin is loud; a quiet Fade is enough.
   :::
